frequency_question: How often does the U.S. execute the specific escalation of sanctioning major Chinese banks for Iranian oil purchases versus issuing waivers or applying lesser enforcement within a defined short window?
membership_rule: Includes formal U.S. Treasury actions (Section 311 or SDN listings) against top-tier Chinese commercial banks for oil-related sanctions evasion; excludes warnings, diplomatic demarches, or actions against small regional/boutique banks.

cases.name: 2019-2020 Peak Iran Sanctions Campaign (Boutique/Shipping entities targeted, major banks spared)

coverage_note: 3 distinct policy windows evaluated; covers all major historical junctures where secondary sanctions on Chinese banks for Iranian oil were actively weighed.
known_gaps: Excludes confidential diplomatic enforcement actions that did not result in public Treasury designations.
skeleton: Major sanction enforcement cycles against China regarding Iranian energy imports since 2012, categorized by whether systemically important Tier-1 banks were designated.
multiplier: 1 hit out of 3 major policy inflection points
validity_reason: Based on structural great-power financial deterrence dynamics which evolve slowly across presidential administrations.
